source_text: XVI. [Β---] οὖν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν βαστάζοντες καὶ ἔθηκαν χαμαὶ παρὰ τὸν βωμόν, ᾧ δὲ παρειστήκει Εὐκτήμων εἰδωλολατρικῶς. καὶ ὁ Λέπιδος εἶπεν· Διὰ τί ὑμεῖς οὐ θύετε, Πιόνιε; οἱ περὶ Πιόνιον εἶπαν· Ὅτι Χριστιανοί ἐσμεν. Λέπιδος εἶπεν· Ποῖον θεὸν σέβεσθε. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς. Λέπιδος εἶπεν· Ὁ οὖν ἐσταυρωμένος ἐστίν; Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ τοῦ κόσμου. οἱ δὲ ἄρχοντες μέγα βοήσαντες ἀνεγέλασαν καὶ ὁ Λέπιδος αὐτῷ κατηράσατο. ὁ δὲ Πιόνιος ἐβόα· Θεοσέβειαν αἰδέσθητε, δικαιοσύνην τιμήσατε, τὸ ὁμοιοπαθὲς ἐπίγνωτε, τοῖς νόμοις ὑμῶν κατακολουθεῖτε· ἡμᾶς κολάζετε ὡς μὴ πειθομένους, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀπειθεῖτε· κολάζειν ἐκελεύσθητε, οὐ βιάζεσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: Then carrying him they brought him and laid him on the ground next to the altar, and beside it Euktemon was standing in an idolatrous way. And Lepidos said: Why do you not sacrifice, Pionius? Those with Pionius said: Because we are Christians. Lepidos said: What god do you worship? Pionius said: The one who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them. Lepidos said: Is it then the crucified one? Pionius said: Whom God sent for salvation of the world. And the rulers, having shouted loudly, laughed out and Lepidos cursed him. And Pionius cried out: Show reverence for godliness, give honor to justice, acknowledge the likeness of suffering, keep to your own laws; you punish us as if disobeying, and you yourselves disobey; you were commanded to punish, not to use force.
pass_b_english: So they carried him in and set him on the ground beside the altar, where Euctemon stood by in idolatrous attendance.

And Lepidus said, “Why do you not sacrifice, Pionius?” Those with Pionius said, “Because we are Christians.” Lepidus said, “What god do you worship?” Pionius said, “Him who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.” Lepidus said, “Is it then the crucified one?” Pionius said, “Him whom God sent for the salvation of the world.” At this the rulers raised a loud shout and burst into laughter, and Lepidus cursed him.
But Pionius cried out, “Show reverence for godliness, give honor to justice, acknowledge that we share your mortal nature, keep to your own laws.
You punish us as men who will not obey, yet you yourselves disobey.
You were commanded to punish, not to compel.”

choices.english: on the ground beside the altar
choices.why: χαμαὶ is adverbial of place and παρὰ with accusative gives proximity, so laid low beside rather than upon the altar

choices.english: recognize that we suffer as you do
choices.why: neuter substantive with ἐπιγιγνώσκω plural imperative addresses shared mortal condition in a forensic appeal, not doctrinal likeness

choices.english: you were ordered to punish, not to compel
choices.why: passive aorist of κελεύω states legal commission while infinitive contrast opposes lawful punishment to coercion to sacrifice
rejected: you were commanded to chastise, not to do violence
